title: Signing requests
description:
Sign requests with HMAC so a server can tell they came from you and were not changed.

```
string to sign:
POST
/v1/orders
1767225600
{"item":"tea","qty":2}
signature: 6f1c…
server check: valid
changed body: invalid
```

starter.main.py:
import hashlib
import hmac

SECRET = b"demo-secret-not-real"


def sign(method, path, timestamp, body):
    return ""


def verify(method, path, timestamp, body, signature, now):
    return False


ts = 1767225600
body = '{"item":"tea","qty":2}'
signature = sign("POST", "/v1/orders", ts, body)
print(verify("POST", "/v1/orders", ts, body, signature, now=ts + 10))

hints: `compare_digest` takes the same time whatever the strings are, so an attacker cannot guess the signature one character at a time.
requirements: The string to sign is the method, path, timestamp and body joined by new lines.
The server side recomputes it and compares with `hmac.compare_digest`; it also refuses timestamps more than 300 s old.
stretch: Put the signature and timestamp in headers and write the request with `urllib.request.Request` (without sending it). This course has not used `Request`: look it up in the `urllib.request` documentation; it takes the URL, `data` (the body as bytes), a `headers` dict and a `method`.
